decision: Accept the proposed static ordinary-domain/cut exclusion for these two events, conditional on the precise Root amendment below before native. Do not add a broad M-local channel, generic header worker or arbitrary factory-input experiment merely to call the frozen negatives executed.

basis.result: The admitted ordinary bridge catch creates the pristine pending B through the original finiteNativePending/Response.json constructor. The same B is registered and returned; the pinned ordinary flow exposes no external B reference or native-header-guard mutator before finish. Freezing a Headers object does not make its internal guard immutable, and replacing B with a fetched/redirect/error response changes the origin/object domain. A same-B immutable transition is therefore excluded only within this exact closed graph. Captured setter failure is guarded, but no general native immutable-header support capability is established.

The original entry stores the awaited bridge result and then runs original synchronous parent.finish followed by synchronous observer.finish in its finally. The async fetch cannot resolve its returned response until finally completes; direct runtime serialization of that return therefore occurs after this cut. There is no deferred observer callback in that finally. The factory has no serialized flag/API and cannot claim to detect a manually staged post-serialization mutable B.

wordingPrecision: The original S03 await forwardFiniteOwnerChoice remains between invocation/bridge completion and entry continuation. Do not claim absence of every await or microtask from caught(B) to finish. The proof relies on absence of external B exposure/mutation in the pinned graph and the synchronous finally-to-fetch-resolution ordering, with actual native direct-route witness still mandatory.
